title: Where poles break
subtitle: Load, taper and the weakest section

chapters.title: Follow the load
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}Where might this pole break? [P1.5] Start with the {CAM:tip}{LABEL:Tip load}sideways load at its physical tip. [P0.8] {CAM:returnWide}Bending demand increases down the pole. The section on the right shows the timber available to resist it.

chapters.title: Demand meets resistance
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}The pole also thickens towards the ground. Demand is only half the story. [P0.4] Here, {CAM:section}{LABEL:Beam utilisation}green and blue show utilisation below the assumed timber strength. [P0.8] Applied stress, material strength and their ratio are different quantities.

chapters.title: A local weakness
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}This pole has a weakened region above ground. [P0.8] {CAM:detail}{LABEL:Remaining timber}Look at the remaining timber. It still carries load. A defect can change the governing height; this close view does not identify it.

chapters.title: Turn the load
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}The load now points in another direction. [P0.8] Follow the {CAM:tip}{LABEL:Load direction}arrow. An off-centre defect can respond differently when bending changes direction. [P0.4] These are beam bending estimates. Splitting, shell instability and real fracture need separate assessment.

title: Decay and pole strength
subtitle: Material, location and the remaining shell

chapters.title: Begin with sound timber
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}An intact surface can conceal deterioration. [P0.8] {CAM:detail}{LABEL:Sound timber}Here the cut face contains sound timber. In bending, fibres farther from the centre have greater leverage. The location of damage therefore matters, as well as its size.

chapters.title: Decay is not always a cavity
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}Decay weakens wood without leaving a hole. [P0.4] {CAM:detail}{LABEL:Prescribed decay}This section has central decay, becoming less severe away from its source. [P0.8] The distribution is prescribed: an illustrative material penalty, not a forecast of decay growth.

chapters.title: Location changes the response
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}The weakened region is now nearer the outside. [P0.8] {CAM:detail}{LABEL:Off-centre decay}The coloured section shows beam utilisation in the remaining material. This case is fixed. Position changes the bending response; this view cannot demonstrate every damage pattern.

chapters.title: A hollow leaves a shell
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}A cavity removes wood completely. [P0.8] {CAM:detail}{LABEL:Remaining shell}The cut face shows the shell left around the opening. Its size and position affect resistance. Thin shells may split or buckle; those failure mechanisms are not predicted by this beam bending model.

chapters.title: Choose an inspection plane
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}Where should we inspect? [P1.5] {CAM:detail}{LABEL:Opposed devices}The U B one thousand pair sits opposite each other at one height. One transmits; the other receives. This scene shows the arrangement. The next view shows the simulated pulse.

chapters.title: Watch the pulse travel
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}A simulated pulse crosses sound wood. [P0.8] {CAM:detail}{LABEL:Received signal}Below, the trace shows the receiver response while the animation repeats. Later waves reflect around the section. Acoustic parameters are illustrative; the colour scale stays the same.

chapters.title: Defects alter the signal
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}Decay changes this simulated response. [P0.8] {CAM:detail}{LABEL:Sound reference}Compare the section trace with the sound reference below. Reflection, scattering and damping can affect the waveform. A large peak alone does not establish strength: overlapping waves can reinforce one another.

chapters.title: From measurement to assessment
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}This number is a {LABEL:Timber bending estimate}timber bending estimate. [P0.8] It uses geometry, material inputs and defects in a separate structural model. {CAM:section}The acoustic animation cannot measure fibre strength. Approved device calibration and interpretation remain separate requirements.

title: Before anyone climbs
subtitle: Condition, demands and an approved decision rule

chapters.title: Look beyond appearance
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}A pole can look sound while hiding deterioration. [P0.8] Appearance is only part of inspection. {CAM:detail}{LABEL:Surface appearance}These outside and cut-face images are model views, not field evidence. A pre-climb assessment must consider more.

chapters.title: Inspect the hidden condition
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}This transparent model exposes entered decay. [P0.8] {CAM:detail}{LABEL:Entered condition}The section shows its position and remaining wood. Ultrasound contributes evidence in practice, requiring reliable measurements and validated interpretation. This geometry is prescribed, not measured acoustically.

chapters.title: Consider the demands
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}The red arrow represents a simple {CAM:tip}{LABEL:Applied load}sideways tip load. [P0.8] It does not depict a climber or all the forces from their equipment. A real assessment must include actual work loads, the planned procedure and ground conditions.

chapters.title: Use the approved procedure
chapters.text: {CAM:whole}Inspection evidence supports an approved work procedure. [P0.8] {CAM:detail}{LABEL:Simulated inspection}This repeating ultrasound view is a teaching simulation. The laboratory has no validated climb decision rules and cannot give clearance. Follow the complete inspection and escalation process.

title: Estimate a pole test load
subtitle: A practical walkthrough: species, dimensions, deterioration and the critical section

chapters.title: Start with the test arrangement
chapters.text: {CAM:ground}What does the test arrangement assume? [P1.5] In Setup, open Ground, then Reference option. Select {LABEL:Ideal fixed groundline}Ideal fixed groundline for a restrained cantilever. {CAM:tip}The model loads the physical tip. Match that fixture; a three-point bending test needs a different model.

chapters.title: Choose the timber and measurements
chapters.text: {CAM:properties}Under Pole, open {LABEL:Properties}Properties. Choose a source appropriate to the timber. {CAM:entered}Here, eight gigapascals and forty megapascals are example assumptions, not measured data. [P0.8] {CAM:dimensions}{LABEL:Entered dimensions}Enter length, embedment and the three diameters or circumferences. Keep the property source with the case.

chapters.title: Describe the known deterioration
chapters.text: {CAM:defects}In Defects, choose a type and press {LABEL:Add}Add. {CAM:cavity}Set its height, length, width and depth. Position and shape controls place this cavity off centre. [P0.8] It removes wood completely. Decay instead leaves weakened material, with an illustrative severity-to-strength relationship.

chapters.title: Read the timber bending estimate
chapters.text: {CAM:capacity}Choose Stresses and {LABEL:Capacity (kN)}Capacity in kilonewtons. Keep Specified load direction, then press {CAM:critical}{LABEL:Critical section}Critical section. [P0.8] Timber bending limit is the whole-pole estimate. The height curve shows section capacities; its lowest value locates the first bending limit, possibly above ground.

chapters.title: Explore direction and uncertainty
chapters.text: {CAM:direction}The compass controls the load direction. [P0.8] {CAM:worst}{LABEL:Worst direction}Load applied in worst direction searches for a weaker orientation. Off-centre damage makes direction important. The comparison also depends on entered dimensions and material strength; credible input ranges are part of interpreting this estimate.

chapters.title: Compare, save and check against a test
chapters.text: {CAM:menu}Open Menu and {LABEL:Compare A/B}Compare A and B to set up matching cases. {CAM:compare}Hold geometry, material and direction constant when comparing deterioration. {CAM:save}Save case preserves the inputs and property source. [P0.8] This beam first-limit estimate is not a validated fracture load; comparison with measured tests remains necessary.

title: UB1000 and the analyser
subtitle: From an inspection plane to a recorded scan

chapters.title: Place the pair
chapters.text: {CAM:devices}Hidden timber condition needs inspection evidence. [P0.8] The {LABEL:UB1000 pair}U B one thousand uses opposed devices to send and receive ultrasound through the pole. {CAM:devicesClose}Here they mark one inspection plane. The laboratory animation is illustrative; it is not a calibrated instrument reading.

chapters.title: Open the analyser
chapters.text: {CAM:analyserHome}The {LABEL:Axonic Analyser}Axonic Analyser prototype organises the inspection around a pole and its scans. [P0.8] {CAM:analyserScan}The scan view brings the devices and acquisition workflow together. In this demonstration, example signals drive the display. No connected instrument or measured field result is implied.

chapters.title: Read the evidence
chapters.text: {CAM:analyserResult}A scan produces evidence to examine, rather than a picture of the exact decay shape. [P0.8] {CAM:analyserDetail}{LABEL:Recorded scan}The analyser keeps scan information available for review. Signal behaviour needs an approved interpretation; a single peak is not a direct measurement of pole bending capacity.

chapters.title: Keep the assessment connected
chapters.text: {CAM:analyserRecords}Records connect the inspection activity with the pole being assessed. [P0.8] {CAM:analyserHome}Keep that evidence alongside material, geometry and structural information. The demonstration shows the workflow, while the laboratory uses a separate bending model. Neither the animation nor these example screens grants climbing clearance.

title: Introducing Safe2Climb
subtitle: A structured inspection and an auditable record

chapters.title: Structure the inspection
chapters.text: {CAM:safeHome}A pre-climb inspection needs a clear sequence and a record of what happened. [P0.8] {CAM:safeChecks}{LABEL:Structured checks}Safe2Climb guides the inspector through the pole, attachments, setting, movement and base condition. Each step keeps observations connected to the inspection, making the process easier to review.

chapters.title: Add another safety layer
chapters.text: {CAM:safeUB}The {LABEL:UB1000 check}U B one thousand check adds another layer of inspection evidence. [P0.8] It supplements the physical checks. {CAM:safeScan}The prototype demonstrates acquisition and follow-up states with example results. Those examples are not live measurements, and they do not replace an approved climbing decision procedure.

chapters.title: Record lean and movement
chapters.text: {CAM:safeLean}{LABEL:Lean record}A lean record can retain a photograph and an indicated pole alignment. [P0.8] {CAM:safeMovement}{LABEL:Movement record}Movement observations can include a recorded amount and a note. Together, these records make the observation clearer for another person. This prototype uses an image angle and manually entered movement.

chapters.title: Make issues visible
chapters.text: {CAM:safeIssues}When something causes concern, record the reason and supporting evidence. [P0.8] {CAM:safeRecords}{LABEL:Inspection record}Inspection history keeps issues visible for review and handover, with the pole and inspection context. That creates an auditable record. This local prototype demonstrates the workflow; it does not send a live network notification.
